evidenceInspected.method: Ordered sampled still sequences inspected directly with view_image; no continuous video watched.

observations.finding: Across ordered samples, red approaches blue while small orange projectiles travel through the arena. Blue reads as a ranged caster and red as a pursuer. Color and repeated spatial behavior create a thin identity, but shared tiny silhouettes and weak visible spell anticipation keep this from feeling like recognizable, characterful mage combat. In A, blue HP is 34 at 5s while red is 90; the consequence reads from the status text much more clearly than the hit itself.

A freezes with red winning at 9.8s; C freezes at 11.9s. B continues through 19.8s. B has a broad blue ground ring around red at 14s, which is one of the stronger distinct visual cues in this sequence. Longer spacing gives room for reading, but these samples do not establish whether the extra time builds tension or merely repeats pursuit. I would not penalize it simply for lasting longer.

Pale blue marks near green/red and multiple orange projectiles near blue/yellow provide more varied magic than the duel. Red stays near green, while blue/yellow occupy the other side. At 8s green is gone in A, at 78 HP in B, and 12 HP in C. This gives the variants distinct consequences and makes red a recognizable threat, although small effects on the grid compete for attention.

B still has all four fighters at 16s, while A has red/yellow and C has red/blue. B shows the large blue ground ring near red at 12s; C shows a similar ring at 16s. Multiple active threats and more surviving specialists make B worth exploring, but survival diversity is not visual quality by itself. A has a legible sequence of red pursuing green, then blue, then yellow; it risks feeling like one repeated answer.

I did not see a surprise that clearly reinterprets an established ability or habit. Repositioning and different elimination order occur, but a viewer cannot reliably connect them to a planted tactical expectation from these sampled sequences. This is a gap for my assigned persona, not proof that such moments never occur.

expectationAssessment.reason: Functional comparison exposes differences, but this persona wants much clearer spell anticipation and visible payoff before endorsing watchability.
